title: Idempotency-Key Implementation Plan
description: A structured plan for an Idempotency-Key endpoint implementation, so the fingerprint-check / in-progress-lock / recovery-point trio and this skill's Quality Gates can be checked deterministically by scripts/idempotency_key_patterns_audit.mjs.

keyGenerator.description: Who generates the idempotency key. Must be the client — a server-generated key cannot survive a network retry.

keySource.description: What the key value is derived from. random-uuid is the only safe choice.

fingerprintCheck.description: True if the request fingerprint (method, path, params) is stored and checked, returning 422/400 when a key is reused with a different body.

inProgressLock.description: True if a lock (locked_at column or Redis SET NX EX) prevents two concurrent retries from both executing the work, with 409 returned to the loser.

lockTtlSeconds.description: Stale-lock TTL covering crashed workers; sized to worst-case request latency (canonical: 90).

recoveryPointStateMachine.description: True if the implementation advances a recovery_point label per atomic phase so a crashed retry resumes mid-flow rather than restarting.

maxSideEffectsPerPhase.description: The maximum number of external side effects committed inside any single atomic phase. Must be at most 1.

statusCodeFlavor.description: Which documented status-code convention the API follows: Stripe (400 on fingerprint mismatch) or IETF draft (422). Never a third invention.

retentionHours.description: How long keys are retained before the reaper deletes them. 24 is the canonical floor.

durableStore.description: Where the durable key record + response cache live. redis-only is lossy and fails the audit.

uniquenessScope.description: Scope of the unique index. Must be per-tenant — (user_id, idempotency_key) — to prevent cross-tenant collisions.

appliesToSafeMethods.description: True if the header is also required on GET/PUT/DELETE. Should be false; those methods are already idempotent.
